title: Python Practice
description: A short module that shows the coding exercises: write a function, then write a loop. Each is checked in the browser.

questions.prompt: What does the keyword `def` do in Python?
How many times does the body of `for i in range(3):` run?

slides.title: A function is a named recipe
slides.body: A function is a small piece of code with a name. You write it once with `def`, then use it as many times as you like by calling its name.

slides.title: Taking something in, giving something back
slides.body:
A function can take values in (its parameters) and hand a value back with `return`.

For example, a function called `double` could take 4 and return 8.

slides.title: return is not print
slides.body:
`return` gives a value back to the code that called the function. `print` only shows text on the screen.

If a function has no `return`, it gives back `None`.

questions.prompt: What does a function give back when it has no `return` line?
questions.explanation: With no return, Python gives back None, which means no value.

activities.title: Write a function: square
activities.body:
Write a function called `square` that takes a number `n` and **returns** that number multiplied by itself.

For example, `square(4)` should give `16`.

Use `return`, not `print`. Press **Check my code** to see which tests pass.

activities.title: Write a loop: count up
activities.body:
Write a program that reads a whole number `n` and prints the numbers from 1 to `n`, one on each line.

For example, if `n` is 3, it prints 1, 2 and 3.

The first line is done for you. Stuck? Press **Need a hint?** and the tutor will look at your code.
activities.starterCode:
n = int(input())

# print the numbers from 1 to n
